text:
/xp - experience progress
/xp takes no arguments and reports your progress from the server, in three lines: your level and the experience standing between you and the next one (with the percentage of the way there), your total experience earned, and your unassigned experience.

Use it in preference to the character panel's "experience to next level" line, which is drawn from a chart the client carries itself and stops being meaningful high up the level range. At the very top of the chart /xp simply names your level and says there is nothing beyond it. See Levels and experience.

/lph - Luminance per hour
/lph reports the Luminance you have earned since you logged in and the rate that works out to per hour. /lph start resets the window and starts counting again from now, which is what you want before timing a particular dungeon or rotation.

The count is per session: it lives only in memory and starts over at every login. Ask again inside a few seconds of the last reading and it will decline to answer - the window is too short for the rate to mean anything.

/bonus, /altbonus, /offlinebonus - experience bonuses
Three read-only readouts. None of them toggles anything: every bonus on DreamWeave switches itself on and off according to your own play.

Command	What it shows
/bonus	The full breakdown - gear, augmentation, alternate character and offline sources listed separately, then how they combine, then the total applied to a kill for both experience and Luminance. It also notes which of them quest experience and allegiance pass-up do not receive.
/altbonus	Whether this character is currently receiving the alternate character catch-up bonus, and the level it is catching up to.
/offlinebonus	How much banked offline bonus time you are holding, and whether it is currently being spent as you fight or banking again because you have been idle.

/pickupspeed - pick-up speed
/pickupspeed reports how much faster you pick things up than a character with no bonus, both as a percentage and as a speed multiplier. Pick-up speed bonuses are permanent quest rewards and can never be lost; the readout tells you when you have reached the highest bonus the server allows.

/quests - quest stamps
/quests shows your own quest stamp count, your account's total, how many stamps stand between you and the next reward tier, and which tiers this character has already claimed. It takes no arguments.

Do not confuse it with retail's /myquests, which is the raw quest log rather than the stamp ledger.

/charsheet - public character sheet
/charsheet publishes a web page for your character at char.acdreamweave.com and prints its link. The sheet shows your level, the gear you are wearing laid out like the in-game paperdoll (click any piece for its full details), your attributes, vitals and trained and specialized skills (each as its base value with the buffed value in brackets), your class abilities and your leaderboard ranks, best placement first. Nobody has a sheet until they ask for one - running the command is what makes yours public, and anyone with the link can then see it.

Command	What it does
/charsheet	Show your sheet's link, creating one if your sheet is not public yet.
/charsheet rotate	Issue a new link. The old link stops working.
/charsheet off	Hide your sheet. Running /charsheet again makes a new link.
You can also switch your sheet on or off from your account page on the Market. The sheet reads your character live, but a change to your gear can take a few minutes to appear.

/abilities - class abilities
The chat front end for Class Abilities. Abilities themselves are bought as training tokens from the class trainers in the Drift Network hall, not from this command.

Command	What it does
/abilities	Your learned abilities, each with its effective value and where it comes from, and your point balance. An ability whose ranks buy two things shows both values.
/abilities all	The full catalogue of abilities, marking which you have learned.
/abilities enhanced [skills|attributes|vitals]	The Enhanced families on their own, by category.
/abilities info <ability>	One ability in detail.
/abilities points	Your points, and the current price of the next point on both purchase lanes.
/abilities buyxp [count]	Buy Class Ability Points with unassigned experience.
/abilities token list	Every training token a trainer sells, with its point cost per rank.
/abilities unlearn <ability>	Refund an ability's points for a Luminance fee. You are asked to confirm first.
A full respec is handled separately - see Class Abilities.

/facet - multiple builds on one character
The chat front end for Player Facets: up to four saved builds on one character, each with its own trained skills, class abilities and worn gear. See that page for the rules, the unlock levels and what each facet keeps.

Command	What it does
/facet	List your four slots - name, which one is active, which are still locked, and a summary of what each holds.
/facet <1-4>	Turn to that facet. The first time you take up a slot it asks you to confirm, because the change strips your worn gear back into your pack and untrains the skills the outgoing build was carrying.
/facet <1-4> trim	Turn to a facet you are short of experience for, giving up just enough of its skill ranks to cover the gap. Plain /facet <1-4> tells you the shortfall and previews the cuts first.
/facet pk [trim]	Turn to your PK facet, on which you are always a player killer and have no class abilities; every other facet is always non-PK. Unlocks at level 150.
/facet name <1-4> <name>	Name a slot, up to 32 characters.
/facet help	Print the rules in game, including the unlock levels currently in force.
Facets are changed in the Marketplace and nowhere else.

/mods - equipment mods
/mods summarises the equipment mods on the armour, clothing and jewellery you are wearing: one line per mod type, with the combined value, how many items carry it, and how close that is to a perfect roll. A mod whose class ability you have not learned is marked inactive.

/mods items shows the same information broken out per item instead, with each item's mod slots used and filled.

/xpaugs, /lumaugs, /augs - augmentations
Two read-only lists of your augmentation progress, each split into complete and incomplete, with a running "X of Y complete" count in the header. Repeatable augmentations show how many of the maximum you hold.

Command	What it shows
/xpaugs	Experience augmentations - the ones bought with experience from the Augmentation Realm.
/lumaugs	Luminance augmentations - the auras, your skill credits, and the aura set of the Seer you are sworn to (or, if you have sworn to none, the four you may choose between).
/augs, /aug	A signpost. /augs xp and /augs lum run the two lists above; on its own it names them both.
Currency and storage

/b, /bank - the Currency Bank
The Currency Bank holds your currency off your character, and is reachable from anywhere. /b on its own shows your balances; /bank on its own prints the command list. Everything else works from either spelling.

Currency codes: p=pyreals, l=luminance, k=legendary keys, pn=promissory notes, n=trade notes, pea=peas.

Command	What it does
/b	Show your balances, your banked offline bonus time, and your alternate character bonus if it is running.
/b d	Deposit everything.
/b d p [amount]	Deposit pyreals - all of them, or an amount like 10k.
/b d l|k|pn|n	Deposit Luminance, legendary keys, promissory notes or trade notes.
/b d pea	Deposit peas as pyreals, at face value.
/b w p <amount>	Withdraw pyreals, paid out as 250,000 trade notes plus loose coin.
/b w n [value] <count>	Withdraw trade notes; the note value defaults to 250,000.
/b w k|pn <amount>	Withdraw legendary keys or promissory notes.
/b t p|k|pn <amount> <character>	Transfer to another character.
/b ad [on|off]	Send vendor sale proceeds straight to the bank, or take them as coin in your pack. With no argument it reports the current setting.
Luminance can be deposited but never withdrawn or transferred - you spend it from the banked balance. Bank commands that move currency are refused while you are trading or otherwise occupied, and cannot be spammed.

/mule - account vault
/mule summons your account's vault vendor beside you. Sell to it to deposit, buy from it to withdraw; every price is zero in both directions. It can only be summoned in the Marketplace, it departs if you wander too far or leave it alone too long, and the vault is shared by every character on your account. See Mule storage for what it accepts and how much it holds.

Command	What it does
/mule	Summon your own vault vendor.
/mule <player>	Summon a vault you have been given access to.
/mule search <text>	Filter the summoned vault vendor to items whose name or spells match. /mule search on its own clears the filter.
/mule search all <text>	Search your own vault and every vault shared with this character. Matches are listed in chat - up to 5 per vault and 25 in all - and nothing is summoned.
/mule search mine <text>	Filter your own vault, even while a friend's vault vendor is the one summoned.
/mule search <player> <text>	Summon that player's shared vault already filtered to <text>.
/mule grant <player> [withdraw]	Let that player deposit into your vault, or deposit and withdraw.
/mule revoke <player>	Remove their access.
/mule access	List who can use your vault.
/mule log	Recent deposits and withdrawals on your vault, and by whom.
/mule upgrade	Buy 100 more vault entries for your account. The price rises each time.
/mule help	Print this list in game.
A name containing a space goes in quotes: /mule grant "Some Player" withdraw.

/market upgrade, /market mine - market listings
Command	What it does
/market upgrade (or /market u)	Buy 10 more market listing slots for your account. The first costs 500 Trade Notes from your banked pyreals and each one after costs 20% more. You confirm the price first, and the slots are permanent.
/market mine [page]	Your active listings, 25 to a page.
Fellowships

/fship
Runs a fellowship from chat, alongside the normal fellowship panel. Fellowships made this way always share experience. On its own, /fship reports your fellowship's name, leader, size and leech-prevention setting, and its join password if it has one.

Command	What it does
/fship create [name]	Start a fellowship, optionally named, with you as leader.
/fship add [player]	Invite a player by name - they get the usual recruit prompt.
/fship join [player] [password]	Join the fellowship a named player is in, if it is open, or if it is closed and you give its join password. A closed one with no password needs an invite.
/fship addlandblock	Invite every unfellowed player in your area at once. Each gets the normal prompt, and the command is rate-limited.
/fship joinlandblock [password]	Join the largest open fellowship in your area, or start one if there is none. With a password, closed fellowships that password opens count too, and the largest open or matching one wins; if there are password-protected fellowships nearby and nothing matches, nothing is started.
/fship password [password|off]	Leader only to set or remove. Setting a password closes the fellowship, and anyone who knows it can join without an invite. On its own, shows any fellow the current password. Opening the fellowship removes it.
/fship list	The fellowships you can join, the ones in your area first. A closed fellowship with a join password is listed and marked as needing one.
/fship noleech [on|off]	Leader only. Drop fellows who stop contributing - see Leech prevention.
/fship quit	Leave your fellowship.
/fship disband	Leader only. Break up the fellowship.
A tell of xp to a fellowship member asks to join their fellowship, the same as /fship join; for a closed fellowship with a password, send xp <password>. A password is one word of up to 32 characters, and capitals do not matter. Five wrong guesses at one fellowship lock you out of guessing it for five minutes. Never use your account password.

An Olthoi character cannot join a fellowship at all.

Combat

/summondamage - summon damage feed
Summoned pets fight on their own and the game says nothing about it, so it is hard to tell whether a summon is contributing. /summondamage on prints one chat line for every hit your own summons land; /summondamage off hides them again, and /summondamage on its own reports which way the switch is set.

The feed is off by default and is remembered per character. You only ever see your own summons - another player's pets are never reported to you, and yours are never reported to them.

/dotdamage - damage-over-time feed
Damage-over-time spells tick away quietly, and on a long fight the chat line for every tick is either the only way to see the spell working or an unreadable wall, depending on how you play. /dotdamage on shows those lines, /dotdamage off hides them, and /dotdamage on its own reports which way you are set and whether that is your own choice or the server's default.

It is your own setting, remembered per character, and it overrides the server default in either direction. It covers only the lines for the ticks you deal; the message telling you that something is ticking on you is not affected.

/fasttick - fast tick
Fast tick gives faster spell release, fast-chugging of potions and food, and melee that sticks to its target. Some players see odd movement or rubber-banding with it, so it is your choice: try it and switch back if it misbehaves.

/fasttick on or /fasttick off sets it for this character.
/fasttick default drops your own choice and follows the server default again.
/fasttick on its own, or /fasttick status, tells you whether it is on and whether that is your own choice or the server's default.
The choice is remembered per character. To change it, stand still and finish what you are doing first - a change is refused mid-action. PK and PKLite characters always run fast tick, whatever they have chosen; the choice is kept and applies again once they are no longer PK.

Travel

/dn, /tn - network recalls
Two recalls into the great hall that holds both travel networks.

/dn recalls to the Drift Network, the DreamWeave hall of portals.
/tn recalls to the traditional Town Network.
Both behave exactly like the Marketplace recall: your name is announced locally, the cast takes about fourteen seconds, and moving too far interrupts it. You cannot call for one while standing in the other - the two halls occupy the same ground, so step outside first.

/exitinstance - leave an instance
/exitinstance returns you from an instanced dungeon to the point you entered from. /exitinst and /leaveinstance do the same thing. Outside an instance it tells you so and does nothing.

/realm - which realm you are in
Dereth is served in more than one realm, and a Thread, an arena or any other private copy is its own instance of one. /realm prints the realm and instance you are standing in.

The same line is printed for you automatically when you log in and whenever a teleport actually moves you to a different realm or instance - not on every portal, only when the answer changes. It is a readout for plugins and for telling one copy from another; nothing about it changes how you play.

Threads

/spawncache - Thread Cache
In a Thread your loot is pooled into a Thread Cache that forms beside you when the run clears. /spawncache is the fallback when it cannot: if you were told there was no room for the cache, move to open ground and type it to form the cache beside you. If a cache has already formed, the command brings it to your side instead, with everything in it.

It works only inside your own Thread and only once the Thread is complete, and it cannot be repeated within a few seconds.

PvP Arena

/arena
Queue for the PvP Arena. You must be on your PK facet.

Command	What it does
/arena join 1v1, /arena join 2v2, /arena join ffa	Queue for that mode.
/arena join 2v2 duo	Queue with your partner; you must be a two-person fellowship.
/arena leave	Leave the queue. Inside a match, it forfeits after you confirm.
/arena status	Whether you are queued, offered a match, or fighting.
/arena accept, /arena decline	Answer a match offer from chat.
/arena rating [name]	Your arena ratings, or another player's.
/top 2v2, /top ffa	The 2v2 and free-for-all ladders, ranked by rating. User-confirmed syntax.
Leaderboards

/top
Every board lists the top 20, and names your own rank underneath if you sit below the cut. Typing /top with no argument prints the menu.

Command	Board
/top dps	Attack arena - highest damage dealt in the 60-second trial.
/top defense	Defense arena - longest survival.
/top wave	Wave gauntlet - highest wave reached, ties broken by the fastest full clear. Each line shows the clear time.
/top speed	Speed trial - fastest run of the current season's dungeon.
/top speed winners	The winner of each of the most recent speed-trial seasons.
/top level	Highest character level.
/top bank	Most pyreals banked. One entry per account rather than per character, listed under its highest-level character, since banked pyreals are pooled across the whole account.
/top cap	Most Class Ability Points earned over a character's lifetime. Spending them costs you no rank.
/top stamp	Most quest stamps earned by a single character.
/top thread	Thread-Guide - highest guide rung cleared, ties broken by lifetime Thread clears. A character with clears but no rung is listed below every rung holder.
/top knot	Best Knot clear: highest Knot level, ties broken by the fastest time from the start of the fight to the kill. Each line shows the Knot, its level and the time.
/top deaths	Most deaths. A character who hides their death count from others is left off.
/top 1v1, /top 2v2, /top ffa	The PvP Arena ladders, ranked by rating.
Staff characters are kept off the boards.
